youtube.title: The Dog Who Saved A Town (True Story)
youtube.description:
In January 1925, diphtheria broke out in Nome, Alaska, and the town's medicine had run out. The sea was frozen, so no ship could bring more, and the planes of the day couldn't fly in that cold. The antitoxin went by train to Nenana, nearly seven hundred miles away, and from there twenty sled-dog teams carried it to Nome like a relay.

Leonhard Seppala's team, led by his twelve-year-old dog Togo, got the hardest part: 170 miles out to meet the medicine, then back again, with a shortcut across the frozen Norton Sound in a blizzard. That night the storm blew the ice they had just crossed out to sea. Togo's team ran 261 miles, far more than any other team. Five and a half days after it set out, the medicine reached Nome and the outbreak was brought under control.

Gunnar Kaasen's team, led by Balto, ran the last 53 miles, and in December 1925 Balto got a statue in Central Park, New York. Togo got his own statue in Seward Park, Manhattan, in 2001: seventy-six years later.

Which dog do you think deserved the statue? 👇
